commands.name: PublishPublisherSet
commands.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published. The command answers when Archicad's API reports the publishing done; for a local or LAN output folder the answer names the folder and lists the files created or changed in it (writtenFiles). A large set can take minutes, so give the call a long enough timeout. The output format of each item is the one set in the publisher set: Archicad's API cannot choose it per call.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set.

outputPath.description: Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.

selectedNavigatorItemIds.description: Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set. Each item wraps its id in navigatorItemId, as the items of GetNavigatorItemTree do: [{"navigatorItemId": {"guid": "6E1C3A9B-0F2D-4B8E-9C7A-1D2E3F405162"}}], not [{"guid": "..."}].

outputFolder.description: The local or LAN folder the set was published to: outputPath, else the path saved in the publisher set. Absent when the set publishes elsewhere (to the Internet or a BIMcloud/Teamwork file server).

writtenFiles.description: Full paths of the files in outputFolder and its subfolders that were created or changed while the command ran, as found when Archicad reported the publishing finished. Absent when outputFolder is absent or holds more than 20000 files and folders.

example.description: Publishes the first publisher set of the project with PublishPublisherSet. Needs at least one publisher set. The output goes to a new temporary folder instead of the path saved in the publisher set; the answer lists the files written there (writtenFiles). Publishing a large set takes long, so the call is given a generous timeout (in seconds).
example.code:
"""Publishes the first publisher set of the project with PublishPublisherSet.

Needs at least one publisher set. The output goes to a new temporary folder instead of the
path saved in the publisher set; the answer lists the files written there (writtenFiles).
Publishing a large set takes long, so the call is given a generous timeout (in seconds).
"""
import tempfile
import aclib

publisherSets = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPublisherSets')['publisherSets']
if not publisherSets:
    raise SystemExit ('No publisher set in the project.')

outputPath = tempfile.mkdtemp (prefix = 'TapirPublish_')
result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('PublishPublisherSet', {
    'publisherSetName': publisherSets[0]['name'],
    'outputPath': outputPath
}, timeout = 600)
aclib.PrintJson (result)
for path in result.get ('writtenFiles', []):
    print ('Written:', path)

commands.name: ModifyDetailMarkers
commands.description: Changes the name, the reference ID, the clip polygon, the boundary's pen and line type, the marker symbol's angle, always-horizontal setting and pen, and 'Copy construction elements only' of Detail and Worksheet markers. Not written: the base point (Archicad places it at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box when the marker is created), the viewpoint the marker refers to, and the marker symbol's other settings, which are parameters of the library part placed as the marker (markerId in GetDetailsOfElements). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.

elementId.description: A Detail or a Worksheet marker.

name.description: The new name of the viewpoint.

id.description: The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker.

clipPolygon.description: The new boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.

polygonArcs.description: Optional arcs of the new boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.

penIndex.description: The new pen of the boundary (API_DetailType::pen).

lineTypeIndex.description: Attribute index of the new line type of the boundary (API_DetailType::ltypeInd).

angle.description: The new rotation of the marker symbol, in radians (API_DetailType::angle).

isHorizontalMarker.description: Whether the marker symbol is always horizontal (API_DetailType::horizontalMarker).

constructionElementsOnly.description: Copy construction elements only (API_DetailType::constructionElementsOnly), as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

markerPenIndex.description: The new pen of the marker symbol, the library part placed as the marker (its markerId in GetDetailsOfElements).

example.description: Changes the ID, name, clip polygon, pens and angle of a Detail marker with ModifyDetailMarkers, reads them back, then deletes it. The script places its own Detail marker on the current floor plan story first (CreateDetailMarkers). ModifyDetailMarkers works on Worksheet markers the same way. penIndex and lineTypeIndex are the boundary's pen and line type, markerPenIndex the pen of the marker symbol; angle turns the marker symbol unless isHorizontalMarker keeps it horizontal. constructionElementsOnly is the marker's 'Copy construction elements only' setting.
example.code:
"""Changes the ID, name, clip polygon, pens and angle of a Detail marker with ModifyDetailMarkers, reads them back, then deletes it.

The script places its own Detail marker on the current floor plan story first (CreateDetailMarkers).
ModifyDetailMarkers works on Worksheet markers the same way. penIndex and lineTypeIndex are the
boundary's pen and line type, markerPenIndex the pen of the marker symbol; angle turns the marker
symbol unless isHorizontalMarker keeps it horizontal. constructionElementsOnly is the marker's
'Copy construction elements only' setting.
"""
import aclib

markers = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateDetailMarkers', {
    'detailMarkersData': [{
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 3.0}],
        'name': 'Wall connection',
        'id': 'D1'
    }]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyDetailMarkers', {
    'detailMarkersWithDetails': [{
        'elementId': markers[0]['elementId'],
        'id': 'D2',
        'name': 'Corner detail',
        'clipPolygon': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 1.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 1.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}],
        'penIndex': 3,
        'lineTypeIndex': 1,
        'markerPenIndex': 5,
        'isHorizontalMarker': False,
        'angle': 0.5,
        'constructionElementsOnly': True
    }]
}))

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': markers})['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']
print (details['detailIdStr'], details['detailName'], len (details['clipPolygon']), round (details['angle'], 3), details['isHorizontalMarker'])

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': markers})

commands.name: CreateLayout
commands.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. A layout that was created but could not be placed is returned with both its databaseId and the error.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.

paperWidth.description: Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.

paperHeight.description: Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.

customLayoutNumber.description: The layout's own number, used when customLayoutNumbering is true. It only replaces this layout's displayed number: the layout still counts in its subset's numbering, so the sheets after it are renumbered. Use doNotIncludeInNumbering to leave it out.

customLayoutNumbering.description: Use customLayoutNumber instead of the automatic number. Does not leave the layout out of the subset's numbering; see doNotIncludeInNumbering.

doNotIncludeInNumbering.description: Leave the new layout out of its subset's automatic numbering, so the numbers of the other sheets do not change.

oneOf.description: The layout was created, but it could not be moved to the place asked for by previousNavigatorItemId or position: it stays where Archicad put it.

example.description: Creates a layout at the end of the Layout Book with CreateLayout, then deletes it again. Needs at least one master layout.

commands.name: ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings
commands.description: Changes the settings of existing Layout Book subsets (name, ID prefix, numbering style, start at, ...), the fields of CreateLayoutSubset; the ones not given keep their value. The Archicad API can neither change the settings of a subset nor delete one, so a new subset is created with the changed settings right after the old one, and the old one's layouts and subsets are moved into it in their order; when a move fails, the ones moved before are moved back. The old subset is left empty, and its id is returned with the new one's: delete it in Archicad. These navigator functions are not undoable.

subsets.description: The Layout Book subsets to change, each with the settings to change.

navigatorItemId.description: The subset to change, from GetNavigatorItemTree or CreateLayoutSubset.

settings.description: The settings to change. The ones not given keep the value the subset has.

subsets.description: One item per input subset, in the same order: the subset that now has the settings and the layouts, and the old subset, left empty, or an error.

navigatorItemId.description: The new subset, with the new settings, holding the layouts and subsets of the old one in their order, right after the old one in the Layout Book.

oldNavigatorItemId.description: The old subset, now empty. The Archicad API cannot delete a subset: delete it in Archicad.

example.description: Changes the ID prefix and numbering of a Layout Book subset with ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings. Creates a subset with one layout first. The command moves the layout into a new subset with the new settings and leaves the old subset empty; the layout and its master are deleted at the end, the two subsets stay in the Layout Book: subsets cannot be deleted through the Archicad API.
example.code:
"""Changes the ID prefix and numbering of a Layout Book subset with ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings.

Creates a subset with one layout first. The command moves the layout into a new subset with the new
settings and leaves the old subset empty; the layout and its master are deleted at the end, the two
subsets stay in the Layout Book: subsets cannot be deleted through the Archicad API.
"""
import aclib

subset = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLayoutSubset', {
    'subsetsData': [{'name': 'Tapir Example Subset', 'addOwnPrefix': True, 'ownPrefix': 'TA', 'numberingStyle': '001', 'startAt': 1}]
})['navigatorItems'][0]
layout = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLayout', {
    'layoutsData': [{'layoutName': 'Tapir Example Layout', 'masterLayoutName': 'Tapir Example Master', 'parentNavigatorItemId': subset['navigatorItemId']}]
})['databases'][0]

changed = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings', {
    'subsets': [{'navigatorItemId': subset['navigatorItemId'], 'settings': {'ownPrefix': 'TB', 'numberingStyle': '01', 'startAt': 10}}]
})['subsets'][0]
aclib.PrintJson (changed)
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLayoutSubsetSettings', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': changed['navigatorItemId']}]}))

# The layout and its master, created above, are deleted again.
layoutBook = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'LayoutBook'})['navigatorItemTree']
master = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLayoutSettings', {'layoutDatabaseIds': [{'databaseId': layout['databaseId']}]})['layoutSettings'][0]['masterNavigatorItemId']
newSubsetGuid = changed['navigatorItemId']['guid'].lower ()
newSubsetItems = [child['navigatorItem'] for child in layoutBook.get ('children', [])
                  if child['navigatorItem']['navigatorItemId']['guid'].lower () == newSubsetGuid]
layouts = newSubsetItems[0].get ('children', []) if newSubsetItems else []
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {
    'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': child['navigatorItem']['navigatorItemId']} for child in layouts] + [{'navigatorItemId': master}]
})

commands.name: CreateDrawings
commands.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

name.description: Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.

nameType.description: Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

position.description: Where the Drawing is placed on the layout, in meters; this becomes its pos. Without clipPolygon it is the lower left corner of the Drawing (before rotation). With clipPolygon it is the point where the origin of the source view lands (on a floor plan the project origin), also when the source view stores its zoom: a model point (x, y) appears at position + scale * drawing scale * (x, y), rotated by angle, and the clipPolygon chooses which part is shown.

scale.description: Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

drawingScale.description: Ignored: Archicad takes the scale from the source view (API_DrawingType::drawingScale is output only). GetDetailsOfElements returns the scale the Drawing got.

modelOffset.description: Offset of the model origin within the drawing, in model meters. Archicad uses it only with clipPolygon and then adds modelOffset * drawing scale (times scale, rotated by angle) to the new Drawing's pos; without clipPolygon it is ignored. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

anchorPoint.description: The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by. Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false; giving anchorPoint makes useOwnOriginAsAnchor default to false. Defaults to Center.

useOwnOriginAsAnchor.description: Whether the drawing is placed by its own origin instead of anchorPoint. Defaults to false when anchorPoint is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

clipPolygon.description: Optional polygon to clip the drawing with, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as position) - not the coordinates of the source view's model. Stored as given: position, angle, scale and modelOffset are not applied to it, and it does not move the content (see position).

commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

items.description: An existing Drawing and the navigator item it should be relinked to.

elements.description: One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

example.description: Places a Drawing of the first story on a layout, then links it to the second story with ChangeDrawingLink. Needs at least two stories and a layout. ChangeDrawingLink recreates the Drawing, so it returns a new element id. Deletes the Drawing at the end.

"""Finds the first named model view option combination by its name with FindModelViewOption, then by its id.

Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

commands.name: SetViewOptions
commands.description: Switches the current plan window to a model view option combination by index, and/or changes the given model view options and on-screen view options. With an index, the model view options stored in the combination apply. The options are read back, and a given field Archicad did not keep (with an index, a given on-screen view option) fails the call with the value it kept; the fields Archicad kept stay changed. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing components shown in the floor plan (modelViewOptions.railing, railing2DDisplayComp*) changed this way, so such a change is reported as not kept; GetViewOptions reads them.

Archicad then applies the model view options stored in the combination: viewOptions.modelViewOptions are not applied together with an index, viewOptions.onScreenViewOptions are. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by name with FindModelViewOption right before switching.

commands.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. example.code:
"""Clones the first story of the Project Map into a new View Map folder with CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap.

Deletes the clone and the folder at the end.
"""
import aclib

def AllItems (item):
    for child in item.get ('children', []):
        yield child['navigatorItem']
        yield from AllItems (child['navigatorItem'])

projectMap = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'ProjectMap'})['navigatorItemTree']
story = next (item for item in AllItems (projectMap) if item['type'] == 'StoryItem')

# A clone must go into a View Map folder, not to the View Map root.
folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder'})
clones = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap', {
    'viewsData': [{'navigatorItemId': story['navigatorItemId'], 'parentNavigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]
})['navigatorItems']
aclib.PrintJson (clones)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [c for c in clones if 'navigatorItemId' in c]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]})

        yield child['navigatorItem']
        yield from AllItems (child['navigatorItem'])

cameraElementId.description: The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.

activeCameraSetElementId.description: The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.

perspective.description: The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.

axonometric.description: The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).

commands.name: Set3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Sets a perspective or an axonometric projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter but sun is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. An axonometry changes only the values given: the projection type, the azimuth, the transformation matrix and the sun. The sun of either changes only the values given in it and is kept when sun is missing. The 3D window shows the change after a rebuild (RebuildView), e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.

axonometry.description: Makes the projection axonometric. Only the given values change, in sun too; the others are kept from the current axonometry, or from the last one when the projection is a perspective.

azimuth.description: The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.

transformationMatrix.description: The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers), as Get3DProjectionSettings returns it. Its 3x3 part must be invertible.

sun.description: The sun position of the axonometry. Only the values given change.

example.description: Raises the camera of the 3D perspective by 1 m and puts its sun at 21 June 13:30, or turns the axonometry to isometric, with Set3DProjectionSettings. The sun of a projection only changes the values given in sun; the others are kept. Restores the original projection at the end.
example.code:
"""Raises the camera of the 3D perspective by 1 m and puts its sun at 21 June 13:30, or turns the axonometry to isometric, with Set3DProjectionSettings.

The sun of a projection only changes the values given in sun; the others are kept.
Restores the original projection at the end.
"""
import copy
import aclib

settings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DProjectionSettings')

if settings['isPersp']:
    # Every perspective parameter but sun is required: pass back what was read, with the camera moved.
    original = copy.deepcopy (settings['perspective'])
    perspective = settings['perspective']

    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Set3DProjectionSettings', {'axonometry': {'projectionType': 'Isometric'}}))

commands.description: Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer.

keepSelection.description: Restore the selection the window had before the command (default). With false the given elements stay selected.

example.description: Zooms the current window to the first three walls with ZoomToElements, keeping the selection as it was. Needs at least one Wall on the current story.
example.code:
"""Zooms the current window to the first three walls with ZoomToElements, keeping the selection as it was.

Needs at least one Wall on the current story.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['OnActualFloor']})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall on the current story.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ZoomToElements', {'elements': walls, 'keepSelection': True}))

commands.name: SetZoom
commands.description: Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates.

zoomBox.description: The area to zoom the current 2D window to, in model coordinates (meters). The window keeps its aspect ratio, so the shown area may be larger than the box. The rotation of the window is kept as it is; in a rotated window the whole box is shown, so the shown area is larger than the box.

example.description: Zooms the current 2D window to the middle of the area it shows now, with SetZoom. Run it with a floor plan, section, worksheet or layout window in front.
example.code:
"""Zooms the current 2D window to the middle of the area it shows now, with SetZoom.

Run it with a floor plan, section, worksheet or layout window in front.
"""
import aclib

# Without parameters GetView2DTransformations returns the zoom of the current window.
zoom = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetView2DTransformations')['transformations'][0]['zoom']
width = zoom['xMax'] - zoom['xMin']
height = zoom['yMax'] - zoom['yMin']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetZoom', {
    'zoomBox': {
        'xMin': zoom['xMin'] + width / 4,
        'yMin': zoom['yMin'] + height / 4,
        'xMax': zoom['xMax'] - width / 4,
        'yMax': zoom['yMax'] - height / 4
    }
}))

commands.name: ResetZoom
commands.description: Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back.

numberOfStepsBack.description: The number of steps to go back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back. The default is 1.

example.description: Fits everything in the current window, then steps back to the previous zoom with ResetZoom, like Zoom Back.
example.code:
"""Fits everything in the current window, then steps back to the previous zoom with ResetZoom, like Zoom Back."""
import aclib

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FitInWindow')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ResetZoom', {'numberOfStepsBack': 1}))

commands.name: CreateSections
commands.description: Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active.

depth.description: The distance of the depth line from the section line, on the left of the start to end direction, which is the direction the section looks in. Default is 1.

id.description: The reference ID shown in the section marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker. Without it the section takes the ID of the Section tool defaults, or none with a favoriteName, as a Section favorite carries no ID.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Section favorite to base the new section on, marker included. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The Section tool defaults are restored afterwards.

example.description: Creates a 10 m long Section on the floor plan with CreateSections, then deletes it again. The section looks to the left of its start to end direction, here to the north.
example.code:
"""Creates a 10 m long Section on the floor plan with CreateSections, then deletes it again.

The section looks to the left of its start to end direction, here to the north.
"""
import aclib

sections = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSections', {
    'sectionsData': [{
        'startCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': -2.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 10.0, 'y': -2.0},
        'depth': 5.0,
        'name': 'Tapir Example Section',
        'id': 'TX-1'
    }]
})['elements']
aclib.PrintJson (sections)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': [s for s in sections if 'elementId' in s]})

commands.name: ModifySections
commands.description: Changes the name and the reference ID of Section and Elevation elements, which the Project Map and the markers show, and moves their section line (startCoordinate, endCoordinate) and depth line (depth, only with the horizontal range Limited, which SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails sets). GetDetailsOfElements reads them back as name, idStr, startCoordinate, endCoordinate and depth.

name.description: The new name, shown in the Project Map.

id.description: The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker.

startCoordinate.description: The new start point of the section line. Only a straight marker (a section line of 2 points, as CreateSections and CreateElevations make) can be moved. The depth line and the marked distant area line keep their distance from it.

endCoordinate.description: The new end point of the section line, as startCoordinate. The view looks to the side the depth line was on.

depth.description: The new distance of the depth line from the section line, on the side it is on. GetDetailsOfElements reads it back as depth. Only applies when the element's horizontalRange is Limited (SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails); refused otherwise.

example.description: Creates a Section with a Limited horizontal range (a depth only applies to one), changes its name and reference ID, moves its end point and its depth line with ModifySections and reads them back. Deletes the section at the end.

commands.name: CreateInteriorElevations
commands.description: Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room.

interiorElevationsData.description: Array of data to create Interior Elevation elements.

example.description: Creates an Interior Elevation around a 5 x 4 m room with CreateInteriorElevations, then deletes it again. Every pair of consecutive points becomes one segment with its own viewpoint; repeating the first point at the end closes the chain.

commands.name: CreateElevations
commands.description: Creates Elevation elements on the floor plan. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active.

id.description: The reference ID shown in the elevation marker and in the Project Map. Without it the elevation takes the ID of the Elevation tool defaults.

example.description: Creates an Elevation on the floor plan with CreateElevations, then deletes it again. The optional 'details' block takes the settings of SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails. The floor plan must be the active window, so the script switches to it first.
example.code:
"""Creates an Elevation on the floor plan with CreateElevations, then deletes it again.

The optional 'details' block takes the settings of SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails. The floor plan
must be the active window, so the script switches to it first.
"""
import aclib

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'windowType': 'FloorPlan'})

elevations = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateElevations', {
    'elevationsData': [{
        'startCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': -5.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 10.0, 'y': -5.0},
        'depth': 20.0,
        'name': 'Tapir Example Elevation',
        'id': 'TE-1',
        'details': {'horizontalRange': 'Limited', 'linePenIndex': 5}
    }]
})['elements']
aclib.PrintJson (elevations)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': [e for e in elevations if 'elementId' in e]})

commands.name: GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails
commands.description: Gets every configurable setting of the given Section and Elevation elements, with their name and reference ID.

example.description: Creates a Section and reads its settings back with GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails. Prints its name, reference ID and ranges, then deletes the section.
example.code:
"""Creates a Section and reads its settings back with GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails.

Prints its name, reference ID and ranges, then deletes the section.
"""
import aclib

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'windowType': 'FloorPlan'})

section = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSections', {
    'sectionsData': [{
        'startCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': -2.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 10.0, 'y': -2.0},
        'name': 'Tapir Example Section',
        'id': 'TX-1'
    }]
})['elements'][0]

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails', {'elements': [section]})['detailsOfElements']
for detail in details:
    aclib.PrintJson ({key: detail.get (key) for key in ('name', 'id', 'horizontalRange', 'verticalRange')})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': [section]})

commands.name: SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails
commands.description: Sets settings of the given Section and Elevation elements: pens, line types, horizontal and vertical range, model effects, story handles and markers. The name and the reference ID are changed with ModifySections.

example.description: Creates a Section, limits its horizontal and vertical range with SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails and reads the settings back. The name and the reference ID are changed with ModifySections instead. Deletes the section at the end.

commands.name: SetInteriorElevationsDetails
commands.description: Sets settings of the given Interior Elevation elements: the stories they are shown on, the common marker's visibility, pen, font and sizes, and for each segment, chosen by its index in GetDetailsOfElements' segments, its name, reference ID and the segment settings of SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails. The element keeps its GUID and its segments keep their viewpoints. A bad segment entry changes nothing on that element, and a change Archicad does not keep (read back after the change) fails the item with the fields it did not apply.

example.description: Creates an Interior Elevation of two segments, shows it on one story only, renames its second segment and limits that segment's vertical range with SetInteriorElevationsDetails, then reads the settings back with GetDetailsOfElements. A segment is chosen by its index in the segments GetDetailsOfElements returns. Deletes the interior elevation at the end.

commands.name: MoveNavigatorItem
commands.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: The new parent of the item. It can be the item's current parent, to change the order of the items in it.

previousNavigatorItemId.description: Optional child of parentNavigatorItemId that the item is placed right after. Without it an item moved within its own parent goes to the end of it.

example.description: Creates two View Map folders and moves the second into the first with MoveNavigatorItem. Deletes both folders at the end.
example.code:
"""Creates two View Map folders and moves the second into the first with MoveNavigatorItem.

Deletes both folders at the end.
"""
import aclib

first = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder A'})
second = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder B'})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MoveNavigatorItem', {
    'navigatorItemIdToMove': second['navigatorItemId'],
    'parentNavigatorItemId': first['navigatorItemId']
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorParentItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': second['navigatorItemId']}]})

# A folder that is not empty cannot be deleted: delete the inner one first.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': second['navigatorItemId']}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': first['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: RenameNavigatorItem
commands.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Renaming the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing also sets the custom name of the Drawing. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

newName.description: The new name of the item. On the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing it is also set as the custom name of the Drawing (nameType CustomName).

newId.description: The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on a Project Map section, elevation, interior elevation, detail or worksheet it is the reference ID of the element behind the item; on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).

customName.description: Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.

example.description: Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem. Deletes the folder at the end.
example.code:
"""Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem.

Deletes the folder at the end.
"""
import aclib

folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateViewMapFolder', {'folderName': 'Tapir Example Folder'})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RenameNavigatorItem', {
    'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId'],
    'newName': 'Tapir Renamed Folder'
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteNavigatorItems', {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': folder['navigatorItemId']}]})

commands.name: DeleteNavigatorItems
commands.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets, View Map folders that are not empty, the other Project Map items and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted; the failed execution result says which case applies. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. dryRun reports the result of the checks made before deleting (item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty) without deleting anything.

dryRun.description: If true, nothing is deleted: each execution result says what the deletion would do for that item, from the checks made before deleting (corrupt id, item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them: a Project Map item other than an independent worksheet, detail or viewpoint created by the Tapir Add-On, a marker-linked worksheet or detail, or in a Teamwork project an item that is not reserved. Default is false.

example.description: Creates an independent Worksheet and deletes it from the Project Map with DeleteNavigatorItems, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

commands.name: GetNavigatorItemTree
commands.description: Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set to retrieve. Used only when navigatorMapId is PublisherSets. Without it the first publisher set is returned.

includeChildCount.description: Set to true to add childCount, the number of direct children Archicad reports, to every item. Defaults to false.

example.description: Prints the Layout Book as an indented tree with GetNavigatorItemTree. The other maps are ProjectMap, PublicViewMap and PublisherSets (with publisherSetName).
example.code:
"""Prints the Layout Book as an indented tree with GetNavigatorItemTree.

The other maps are ProjectMap, PublicViewMap and PublisherSets (with publisherSetName).
"""
import aclib

def PrintTree (item, indent):
    print ('  ' * indent + '{} {} ({})'.format (item['uiId'], item['name'], item['type']))
    for child in item.get ('children', []):
        PrintTree (child['navigatorItem'], indent + 1)

tree = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetNavigatorItemTree', {'navigatorMapId': 'LayoutBook'})['navigatorItemTree']
PrintTree (tree, 0)

commands.name: GetSchedules
commands.description: Returns the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map: navigator item id, name, ID and the folders they are in. Archicad's API does not give the rows of a schedule nor export it; to export one, put it in a publisher set with a spreadsheet format in Archicad and run PublishPublisherSet.

schedules.description: The Interactive Schedules of the Project Map, in navigator order.

name.description: The name of the schedule.

uiId.description: The ID of the schedule, shown before its name in the navigator.

folderPath.description: The names of the Project Map items the schedule is in, from the top down, without the project itself (e.g. Schedules, Element). Archicad's API does not say whether a schedule lists elements, components or surfaces; the default Project Map shows it by these folders.

example.description: Lists the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map with GetSchedules. Each line shows the folders the schedule is in, its ID and its name.
example.code:
"""Lists the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map with GetSchedules.

Each line shows the folders the schedule is in, its ID and its name.
"""
import aclib

schedules = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSchedules')['schedules']
for schedule in schedules:
    print ('{} | {} {}'.format (' / '.join (schedule['folderPath']), schedule['uiId'], schedule['name']))

commands.name: GetNavigatorParentItems
commands.description: Returns the parent of each given navigator item: the folder, subset or layout book item it is in. The root of a map has no parent and gets an error.

parentItems.description: The parent of each requested navigator item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item whose parent cannot be read.

example.description: Prints the folder each View Map view is in, with GetNavigatorParentItems.

commands.name: SetMasterLayoutContext
commands.description: Sets which layout's context the master layout of the current window is drawn in: its autotexts then show the values of the given layout. The current window must be a master layout, otherwise an error is returned. It does not assign a master layout to a layout. Available from Archicad 27.

example.description: Opens the first master layout and draws it in the context of the first layout with SetMasterLayoutContext. Its autotexts then show the values of that layout. Needs a layout and a master layout. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Opens the first master layout and draws it in the context of the first layout with SetMasterLayoutContext.

Its autotexts then show the values of that layout. Needs a layout and a master layout.
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

databases = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDatabases', {'types': ['Layout', 'MasterLayout']})['databases']
layouts = [d for d in databases if d['type'] == 'Layout']
masters = [d for d in databases if d['type'] == 'MasterLayout']
if not layouts or not masters:
    raise SystemExit ('The project needs a layout and a master layout.')

# The current window must be a master layout.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'databaseId': masters[0]['databaseId']})
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMasterLayoutContext', {'layoutDatabaseId': layouts[0]['databaseId']}))

commands.name: GetAddOnViewpointRoots
commands.description: Returns the roots of the add-on viewpoints: the Project Map items created through the Archicad API by an add-on, as Archicad lists them to Tapir. Available from Archicad 27.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of an add-on viewpoint item.

example.description: Lists the roots of the add-on viewpoints (Project Map items made by add-ons) with GetAddOnViewpointRoots. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:

import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAddOnViewpointRoots'))

commands.description: Returns the direct children of an add-on viewpoint root or group. Available from Archicad 27.

viewpointId.description: The add-on viewpoint root or group to list the children of.

example.description: Lists the direct children of every add-on viewpoint root with GetAddOnViewpointChildren. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: GetAddOnViewpoints
commands.description: Returns the details of the given add-on viewpoint items: their parent, type (Root, Group or Leaf), ID, name, view settings flags and attached data (base64 encoded). The output is aligned with the input array; an item that cannot be read gets an error. Available from Archicad 27.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of an add-on viewpoint item.

viewpoints.description: The details of each given add-on viewpoint item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that cannot be read.

roots = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAddOnViewpointRoots')['viewpointIds']

commands.name: CreateAddOnViewpoints
commands.description: Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.

parentViewpointId.description: The root or group to create the item in. Required for a group or a leaf node, ignored for a root.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of a leaf node, as Archicad stores them (a bit field). Ignored for a root or a group.

data.description: Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded.

viewpoints.description: The identifier of each created item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that could not be created.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the created add-on viewpoint item.

example.description: Creates an add-on viewpoint root with a leaf node in it, using CreateAddOnViewpoints. The new items stay in the Project Map. Roots can't be created in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: ChangeAddOnViewpoints
commands.description: Changes the ID, name, view settings flags or attached data (base64 encoded) of the given add-on viewpoint items; only the given fields are changed. Roots and groups can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.

viewpoints.description: The add-on viewpoint items to change. Only the given fields are changed.

example.description: Renames the first add-on viewpoint root with ChangeAddOnViewpoints, reads it back, then restores its name. Needs an add-on viewpoint. Roots can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: ReorderNavigatorItems
commands.description: Reorders the children of a navigator item to match the given order. Works around MoveNavigatorItem being unable to reposition an item within its current parent, by bouncing it through a sibling folder, or through the parent's own parent when no sibling can host it (for example a folder with only views and clone folders).

parentNavigatorItemId.description: The folder whose children should be reordered.

orderedNavigatorItemIds.description: The complete, desired order of every child of parentNavigatorItemId. Every current child must be listed.

example.description: Creates a View Map folder with two subfolders and swaps their order with ReorderNavigatorItems. Deletes the folders at the end.

ElementIdOrError.description: An element identifier or an error.

ElementIdsOrErrors.description: A list of element identifiers or errors.

ModelViewOptionId.description: The identifier of the model view option combination.

ViewOptions.description: The model view options and the on-screen view options, every field by its API_ViewOptions name. Values are the numeric API constants; attribute indices are plain integers.

modelViewOptions.description: Fields of API_ModelViewOptions, with the curtainWall, stair and railing parts as nested objects.

ViewOptionsUpdate.description: The fields to change, named as in the response of GetViewOptions. Fields not given keep their current value. Without an index, the window then uses Custom model view options (index 0), also when only on-screen view options are given. To keep the combination, give its index as well. The options are read back, and a given field Archicad did not keep fails the call with the value it kept.

railing.description: The railing options to change; the ones left out keep their value. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing2DDisplayComp* fields, which SetViewOptions then reports.

RailingModelViewOptions.description: The railing options of the model view options (API_RailingModelViewOptions; Model View Options > Railing Options), every field by its API name: the railing components shown in the floor plan and the schematic 3D display. GetViewOptions and GetModelViewOptionDetails return all of them; SetViewOptions takes any of them and reads them back. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing2DDisplayComp* fields changed through ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions, so SetViewOptions reports such a change as not kept.

railing3DDetailLevel.description: The detail level of railings in the 3D display, the numeric API constant.

railing2DDisplayCompPosts.description: Whether the posts are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompTopRail.description: Whether the top rails are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompHandrails.description: Whether the handrails are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompRails.description: Whether the rails are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompInnerPosts.description: Whether the inner posts are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompBalusters.description: Whether the balusters are shown in the floor plan.

railing2DDisplayCompPanels.description: Whether the panels are shown in the floor plan.

railingSchemeSurfaceIndex.description: The index of the surface used by the schematic 3D display.

railingSchemeCutLineIndex.description: The index of the line type of the cut lines of the schematic 3D display.

railingSchemeCutLinePenIndex.description: The pen of the cut lines of the schematic 3D display.

railingSchemeUncutLineIndex.description: The index of the line type of the uncut lines of the schematic 3D display.

railingSchemeUncutLinePenIndex.description: The pen of the uncut lines of the schematic 3D display.

renovationFilterId.description: Identifier of the renovation filter. The same identifier is the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings.

name.description: Name of the renovation filter.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item.

parentViewpointId.description: The identifier of the root or group the item is in. Missing when Archicad reports no parent, as for a root.

itemType.description: Whether the item is a root, a group or a leaf node.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).

data.description: The data the add-on attached to the item, base64 encoded. Empty when there is none.

viewpointId.description: The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item to change.

displayId.description: The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.

displayName.description: The name shown for the item in the Project Map.

viewSettingsFlags.description: The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).

data.description: Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded. It replaces the attached data; an empty string removes it.

PolyArc.description: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.

begIndex.description: Node index of one end point of the arc.

endIndex.description: Node index of the other end point of the arc.

arcAngle.description: Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

AxonometryProjectionType.description: The projection type of an axonometric 3D projection, the projMod of the Archicad API. Archicad works out the transformation matrix of every type but Custom from the type and the azimuth. XY is the top view and Bottom the view from below. YZ and XZ are both the side view (an elevation), looking from the azimuth. Frontal, Monometric, Isometric and Dimetric are the predefined axonometries, and FrontalBottom, MonometricBottom, IsometricBottom and DimetricBottom the same seen from below; an Isometric at azimuth 270 is the isometric from the south-east (X axis at -30 degrees, Y at 30, Z at 90). Custom keeps the transformation matrix as given. Parallel cannot be set: Archicad makes it Custom.

PerspectiveProjectionParameters.description: The parameters of a perspective projection of the 3D window.

targetPosition.description: The position of the target point the camera looks at.

distance.description: The distance between the camera and the target.

azimuth.description: The azimuth of the camera in degrees: the direction from the target to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis. Archicad works it out from the camera and target positions, so a set value is replaced by that.

viewCone.description: The view cone angle of the camera in degrees.

rollAngle.description: The roll angle of the camera.

isTwoPointPersp.description: True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).

sun.description: The sun position of the perspective. Get3DProjectionSettings always returns it; Set3DProjectionSettings changes only the values given and keeps the current sun when it is missing.

ProjectionSunSettings.description: The sun position of a 3D projection, the Sun Position of the 3D Projection Settings dialog (API_SunAngleSettings). Each perspective and axonometry has its own, independent of the project's date and time (SetSunSettings). The 3D shading and shadows of the projection come from it.

sunPositionOption.description: Angles: the sun is at sunAzimuth and sunAltitude. DateAndTime: Archicad calculates the sun from the project location and the date and time given here.

sunAzimuth.description: The azimuth of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.

sunAltitude.description: The altitude of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.

year.description: Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.

month.description: Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.

day.description: Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.

summerTime.description: True when the time is daylight saving time.

SuccessfulExecutionResult.description: The result of a successful execution.

FailedExecutionResult.description: The result of a failed execution.

DrawingNameType.description: How the drawing's title name is assembled (Identification tabpage of the Drawing Settings dialog).

DrawingAnchorPoint.description: The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by (API_DrawingType::anchorPoint). Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false.

NavigatorItemType.description: The type of the navigator item.

nodeCoordinates.description: The corner points of the connected segment chain. Each consecutive pair of points becomes one segment, so a room with four walls needs five points to be closed, or four to be left open.

depth.description: How far each segment looks. Applied to every segment. Defaults to 1.0.

name.description: Name of the interior elevation. Each segment is named after it.

id.description: ID string of the interior elevation.

floorIndex.description: The story to place the interior elevation on. Defaults to the current story. Archicad places an interior elevation on the active story, so for another story that story is activated while the interior elevation is created, and the previously active one is put back afterwards.

StoredGDLParameter.description: A GDL parameter as it is stored with a marker or a Favorite, read without a parameter interface (so without isLocked and possibleValues).

name.description: The name of the parameter.

displayName.description: The display name of the parameter.

dimension1.description: The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).

dimension2.description: The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).

valueDescription.description: The value description for numeric parameter.

itemDescriptions.description: Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter, one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

NavigatorItemIds.description: A list of navigator item identifiers.

NavigatorItemId.description: The identifier of a navigator item.

NavigatorItem.description: A navigator item and the subtree below it.

name.description: The name of the navigator item.

autoTextedName.description: The name of the navigator item as it was given, with its autotext tokens (e.g. <PROJECTNUMBER>_<SourceID>_<SourceItemName>), while name holds it with the tokens resolved. Only present when the two differ, that is when the name contains autotext.

prefix.description: The floor number for story items, an empty string for every other item type.

uiId.description: The identifier shown next to the name on the navigator.

customUiId.description: True when the identifier was typed by hand instead of being inherited from the Project Map source - the View Settings ID "Custom" radio button.

customName.description: True when the name was typed by hand instead of being inherited from the Project Map source - the View Settings name "Custom" radio button.

isIndependent.description: True when the item is independent, that is when its link to the Project Map is broken.

sourceNavigatorItemId.description: The identifier of the navigator item this one was created from: the Project Map item behind a view, or the source view behind a placed Drawing's Layout Book entry. Missing when the item has no such source; Project Map items never do.

childCount.description: The number of direct children Archicad reports for the item. Only present when GetNavigatorItemTree is called with includeChildCount true.

children.description: The children of the navigator item. Missing when the item has no children.

ViewSettings.description: The settings of a navigator view

modelViewOptions.description: The name of the model view options. If empty, the view has custom model view options.

layerCombination.description: The name of the layer combination. If empty, the view has custom layer combination.

dimensionStyle.description: The name of the dimension style (a dimension standard of Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions, as GetDimensionStandards lists them). If empty, the view has custom dimension style. GetViewSettings returns the name the view stores as it is: Archicad does not check it against the project's dimension standards, so it can name one that GetDimensionStandards does not list, e.g. a standard that was renamed or deleted after the view was saved. It is valid data only when saveFlags.dimensions is true; otherwise the view does not store dimension settings and the name may be a leftover. Use FindDimensionStandard to tell whether the name exists in the project (it fails when it does not).

penSetName.description: The name of the pen set. If empty, the view has custom pen set.

graphicOverrideCombination.description: The name of the graphic override combination. If empty, the view has custom graphic override combination.

drawingScale.description: The drawing scale stored on the view, if enabled (see saveFlags.drawingScale). Giving it to SetViewSettings also turns saveFlags.drawingScale on, unless that flag is given explicitly.

saveZoom.description: Whether the zoom box is stored in the view. The same flag as saveFlags.zoom, kept for compatibility; in SetViewSettings saveFlags.zoom wins when both are given.

ignoreSavedZoom.description: Whether changing to the view should ignore its stored zoom.

zoom.description: Stored zoom box. Used only when saveZoom is true. Giving it to SetViewSettings also turns saveFlags.zoom on, unless that flag is given explicitly.

saveFlags.description: Which settings the view stores: the "stored in this view" checkboxes of the View Settings dialog. A stored setting whose name field is empty is a custom (unnamed) one; a setting that is not stored is not part of the view at all, which the name fields alone cannot tell apart. Always complete in a GetViewSettings response. In SetViewSettings every flag is optional, a flag that is not given keeps its current value, and a flag given here overrides the one implied by drawingScale, zoom, structureDisplay or saveZoom.

zoom.description: Whether the zoom box is stored in the view.

displayOptions.description: Whether the model view options are stored in the view (named by modelViewOptions, custom if that is empty).

layers.description: Whether the layer settings are stored in the view (named by layerCombination, custom if that is empty).

drawingScale.description: Whether the drawing scale is stored in the view.

dimensions.description: Whether the dimension settings are stored in the view (named by dimensionStyle, custom if that is empty). When false, dimensionStyle is not valid data.

penSet.description: Whether the pen set is stored in the view (named by penSetName, custom if that is empty).

structureDisplay.description: Whether the structure display mode is stored in the view.

rotation.description: View rotation angle in radians, derived from transformationMatrix. Read via GetViewSettings; use SetViewRotation to change it.

transformationMatrix.description: The full 2D transformation of the view that rotation is derived from: the 3x4 matrix row by row (12 numbers), in the layout Get3DProjectionSettings uses. Its translation is at indices 3 and 7. Read via GetViewSettings; SetViewSettings ignores it, use rotation or SetViewRotation to change the rotation and translation to change the translation.

translation.description: SetViewSettings only: the translation part of the view transformation (indices 3 and 7 of transformationMatrix), so that view coordinates = rotation applied to model coordinates + translation. rotation leaves the translation as it is; without this field the translation is not changed. {x: 0, y: 0} clears it. Never returned by GetViewSettings (read it from transformationMatrix).

structureDisplay.description: Structure display mode. One of EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes, StructureOnly.

renovationFilterGuid.description: Identifier of the renovation filter applied to the view.

renovationFilterName.description: Name of the renovation filter applied to the view (GetRenovationFilters lists them). GetViewSettings returns it together with renovationFilterGuid when the name could be resolved. SetViewSettings sets the filter by this name (an exact match first, else a case-insensitive one); a name the project has no filter for, or one that names another filter than a renovationFilterGuid given with it, fails the item and nothing of it is written.

d3styleName.description: Name of the 3D style. Empty if not set.

renderingSceneName.description: Name of the rendering scene. Empty if not set.

usePhotoRendering.description: Whether photo rendering is used for this view.

zoom.description: The current zoom parameters. In a rotated window (rotation is not 0) the box is in the window's own rotated frame, as Archicad stores it, not in model coordinates.

InteriorElevationSegmentSettableDetails.description: The changes to one segment of an Interior Elevation, for SetInteriorElevationsDetails. Only the fields given are changed.

segmentIndex.description: The index of the segment in the segments that GetDetailsOfElements returns for the interior elevation, from 0.

name.description: The new name of the segment, shown in the Project Map.

id.description: The new reference ID of the segment, shown in its marker and in the Project Map.

settings.description: The segment settings to change (API_SectionSegment), with the keys of SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails. showOnStories, storyToShowOn and markerShowType are not settings of a segment and are refused here; showOnStories and storyToShowOn are set on the interior elevation itself.

showOnStories.description: Which stories the interior elevation is shown on.

storyToShowOn.description: The story index the interior elevation is shown on, if showOnStories is 'OneStory'.

useCommonMarker.description: Whether the common marker of the interior elevation is shown.

commonMarkerPenIndex.description: Pen index of the common marker.

commonMarkerFontIndex.description: Font index of the common marker.

commonMarkerTextSize.description: Size of the common marker's text.

segments.description: The segments to change, each chosen by its segmentIndex. Segments not listed are kept as they are.

xMin.description: The minimum X value of the zoom box.

yMin.description: The minimum Y value of the zoom box.

xMax.description: The maximum X value of the zoom box.

yMax.description: The maximum Y value of the zoom box.

BoundingBox2D.description: A two-dimensional bounding box defined by its minimum and maximum coordinates.

LayoutInsertionPosition.description: Position of a new layout among its parent's children.

PartialStructureDisplay.description: The Partial Structure Display mode of the current window.

CutPlane.description: A 3D cut plane: the points where pa*x + pb*y + pc*z = pd. The side its normal vector (pa, pb, pc) points to is cut away.

pa.description: Coefficient of x in the plane equation. The x coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pb.description: Coefficient of y in the plane equation. The y coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pc.description: Coefficient of z in the plane equation. The z coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pd.description: The right-hand side of the plane equation, in meters: with a unit normal vector, the distance of the plane from the origin along the normal vector. A plane at y = 2 cutting away y > 2 is pa 0, pb 1, pc 0, pd 2.

cutPen.description: The pen of the edges cut by this plane, from 1 to 255. Get3DCutPlanes leaves it out when the plane has no valid pen (pen 0, set by earlier versions of Set3DCutPlanes).

cutSurfaceId.description: The surface the 3D window draws the faces cut by this plane with. Get3DCutPlanes leaves it out when the plane has no surface attribute (surface 0 draws them black).

name.description: The name of the database. Missing when the database info cannot be read.

referenceId.description: The reference id of the database. Missing when the database info cannot be read.

model3D.description: The 3D model type: Block, Wireframe, Hidden Line or Shading, as the integer value of API_3DModelTypeID.

monochromeEnabled.description: The model is shown in monochrome colors.

monochromeSurfaceColor.description: The surface color of the monochrome model.

monochromeContourColor.description: The contour color of the monochrome model.

backgroundAsInRendering.description: The background is the same as in the rendering settings.

chainBackgroundColors.description: The sky and the ground background colors are chained.

backgroundSkyColor.description: The sky color of the background (API_3DStyle.bkgSkyColor).

shadingContours.description: The contours in shaded mode, as the integer value of API_ShadingContoursID.

vectorialSunShadow.description: The vectorial sun shadow options, as the integer value of API_VectorShadowID.

contourThickness.description: The thickness of the contours, in pixels.

silhouetteThickness.description: The thickness of the silhouettes, in pixels.

vectorialHatchingThickness.description: The thickness of the vectorial hatching, in pixels.

shadowContourThickness.description: The thickness of the shadow contours, in pixels.

castShadowPercent.description: The intensity of the cast shadows, in percent.

shadingPercent.description: The intensity of the shading, in percent.

shadowElevation.description: The elevation of the shadow plane, used by the one level vectorial sun shadow options.

contentBox.description: The full boundary box of the Drawing's content, independent of its frame, as returned by Archicad.

name.description: The name of the subset.

ownPrefix.description: The subset's own ID prefix. Giving it also switches addOwnPrefix on, unless addOwnPrefix is given.

customNumber.description: The subset's custom number (its custom ID). Giving it also switches customNumbering on, unless customNumbering is given.

numberingStyle.description: The ID appearance style of the subset.

startAt.description: The number the subset's numbering starts at.

continueNumbering.description: Whether the subset continues using the ID assignment of the levels above.

useUpperPrefix.description: Whether the subset uses the prefix and IDs of the levels above.

includeToIDSequence.description: Whether the subset is included in the ID sequence: the opposite of the Subset Settings dialog's "Do not include this Subset in ID sequence".

customNumbering.description: Whether the subset has a custom ID (customNumber) instead of an automatically generated one.

addOwnPrefix.description: Whether the subset adds its own prefix (ownPrefix).

navigatorItemId.description: The Project Map item of the new database, for ChangeWindow or CreateDrawings. Missing when the item could not be found.

begC.description: The start point of the line, in layout coordinates.

endC.description: The end point of the line, in layout coordinates.

lineTypeIndex.description: The index of the line type of the line.

Document3DPlanConnection.description: The connection of the 3D Document to the model.

Document3DBoundaryDisplay.description: How the boundary contours are displayed.

Document3DAttributeOptions.description: The uniform attribute options (cut and uncut surfaces, shading, hidden edges).

shouldUseUniformCutAttributes.description: Use uniform attributes on the cut surfaces.

uniformLineType.description: The index of the uniform line type of the cut surfaces.

uniformFillPen.description: The uniform fill pen of the cut surfaces.

uniformFillBkgPen.description: The uniform fill background pen of the cut surfaces.

uncutSurfaceBkgPen.description: The background pen of the uncut surfaces.
